meta.audience: Ammon's brethren, the sons of Mosiah
meta.location: Among the Lamanites, at the end of the mission
meta.unit: The sons of Mosiah among the Lamanites (Alma 17–26)
principles: Joy that keeps its accounting straight

world_behind.title: This is the end of a fourteen-year mission
world_behind.text: Alma 17 began with the brothers separating; here they are together, counting what happened. The speech is a report delivered to the men who did the work.

world_behind.title: Ammon is quoting Alma's conversion
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has the Lamanites in the darkest abyss brought to behold the marvelous light of God. Mosiah 27 has Alma using the same two phrases of himself, and Ammon was in the room.

world_behind.title: Aaron interrupts
world_behind.text: Verse 10 has him rebuke his own brother mid-speech for boasting. The record keeps the objection and then gives Ammon twenty-five verses of answer.

world_behind.title: Their errand had been laughed at
world_behind.text: Verses 23 and 24 recall the Nephites in Zarahemla mocking the plan and listing the Lamanites' crimes as proof it would fail. Verse 25 says some proposed extermination instead.

world_behind.title: They nearly quit
world_behind.text: Verse 27 says their hearts were depressed and they were about to turn back. The comfort that came was a promise of success attached to a command to bear afflictions patiently.

world_behind.title: The abuse is itemized
world_behind.text: Verse 29 lists being cast out, mocked, spit upon, struck on the cheeks, stoned, bound with cords, and jailed. Alma 23 had banned the same list by decree, item for item.

world_behind.title: Ammon ranks the converts above his own nation
world_behind.text: Verses 33 and 34 say no such love exists in the land, not even among the Nephites, because the Nephites would fight rather than be killed.

words.text: A curved blade for reaping grain. The word appears once in this record and twelve times in the King James Bible, most of them in harvest judgments. Ammon's line about thrusting in the sickle into a ripe field is nearly the wording of the angel in Revelation 14.

Wishes, pleases, chooses. An archaic form used five times in this record and twice in the King James Bible, where the wind blows where it listeth. Ammon uses it of the enemy's winds, which cannot carry away the people gathered into God's garners.

Without equal. The record uses it eight times and the King James Bible never. Four of the eight are king Benjamin and his son on the matchless power of God; Ammon attaches it instead to bounty, and to love.

One who repents. It appears seven times in this record and never in the King James Bible. Ammon makes it the entire qualification for knowing the things he has been describing, and verse 22 spells out what a penitent person actually does.
Being deprived of what one needs. The word occurs once in scripture. Ammon uses it to sum up fourteen years in one noun, then immediately lists the specifics in the next verse.

The inward parts, and in scripture the seat of compassion. The record uses it eight times and the King James Bible thirty-nine, always in this sense of felt mercy. Ammon ends the chapter with God's bowels of mercy over all the earth.

phrases.term: Behold the number of your sheaves
phrases.text: Ammon tells his brethren to look at the count. He has just described the field as ripe and the labor as all day long, and now he directs their attention to the result, which is a number of people.

phrases.term: I fear that thy joy doth carry thee away unto boasting
phrases.text: Aaron's whole contribution to the chapter, and it is a correction of his brother in front of the company. The record preserves the rebuke and lets Ammon answer it at length.

phrases.term: I know that I am nothing
phrases.text: The center of the answer. Ammon concedes his own weakness in five words and then says he will boast of God, in whose strength he can do all things. Verse 36 comes back and accepts the word boasting on those terms.
Alma 5 had asked the people of Zarahemla whether they could still sing that song. Here Ammon reports thousands of Lamanites doing it, loosed from the pains of hell.

phrases.term: I cannot say the smallest part which I feel
phrases.text: Ammon stops in the middle of the praise to say the praise is inadequate. He has just asked who can glory too much in the Lord, and he answers his own rhetoric by admitting the language will not stretch.

phrases.term: There is none that knoweth these things, save it be the penitent
phrases.text: How knowing works, in this chapter, stated flatly. Knowledge of these things is restricted, and the gate is repentance. Verse 22 lists the requirements: repentance, faith, good works, and prayer without ceasing.
What their own people did when they announced the mission. Ammon recalls it exactly, including the argument that the Lamanites were too stiffnecked and too bloody to reach.

phrases.term: Bear with patience thine afflictions, and I will give unto you success
phrases.text: The comfort given at the point of turning back. The promise of success arrives bound to a requirement of patience under affliction, and the next verses show which came first.

phrases.term: We have traveled from house to house, relying upon the mercies of the world
phrases.text: Ammon corrects himself in the same breath, adding that it was the mercies of God they leaned on. The self-correction is left in the record, the way Mormon's is in Alma 24.

phrases.term: Has there been so great love in all the land? ... not, even among the Nephites
phrases.text: Ammon puts converted Lamanites above his own nation on the one measure he thinks counts. Verse 34 gives his reason: the Nephites would take up arms and refuse to be slain.

Ammon's name for his own people, a branch lost from the tree of Israel. He has spent the chapter on Lamanites and ends by putting Nephites in the same category, and then extends God's mindfulness to every people in every land.

verses.label: v. 1–7
verses.title: The harvest
verses.text: Ammon asks what blessings they have received, answers his own question, and gives the picture: a ripe field, a thrust sickle, sheaves gathered into garners where storm and whirlwind cannot reach them. They are in the hands of the Lord of the harvest.

verses.label: v. 8–12
verses.title: The rebuke, and the answer
verses.text: He calls for singing and says the Lamanites would still be racked with hatred if the brothers had stayed home. Aaron warns him about boasting. Ammon says his joy is full, that he is nothing, and that he boasts of God, in whose strength he can do all things.

verses.label: v. 13–16
verses.title: Glory
verses.text: Thousands loosed from the pains of hell and the chains of hell, brought from everlasting darkness into everlasting light and encircled with the matchless bounty of God's love. He asks who can glory too much, and admits he cannot say the smallest part he feels.

verses.label: v. 17–22
verses.title: Snatched, and who can know
verses.text: He asks why God did not destroy men who went out in wrath to wreck his church, and says his soul almost flees at the thought. Then the rule: no natural man knows these things, only the penitent, and to such it is given to know mysteries and bring thousands to repentance.

verses.label: v. 23–27
verses.title: Scorn, and comfort
verses.text: He recalls the mockery at Zarahemla, the catalogue of Lamanite wickedness, and the proposal to kill them all. They came with the intent of saving a few. When they were about to turn back, the Lord promised success on the far side of patience.

verses.label: v. 28–31
verses.title: What it cost
verses.text: Every privation, house to house, taught in houses, streets, hills, temples, and synagogues; cast out, mocked, spit on, struck, stoned, bound, jailed, delivered. They had hoped for some souls, and now they look at the fruits and call them many.

verses.label: v. 32–37
verses.title: The love, and the reach of God
verses.text: The converts would die before killing and have buried their weapons deep. No such love exists in the land, not even among the Nephites. Ammon accepts the charge of boasting on his own terms and ends with God mindful of every people, numbering them, his mercy over all the earth.

chapter.title: The rebuke stays in the record
chapter.text: Aaron's warning could have been edited out of a psalm of triumph, and Mormon keeps it. The chapter works as an exchange between two brothers who disagree about how to talk.

chapter.title: Ammon redefines the word instead of denying the charge
chapter.text: He grants that he is nothing and claims all the strength as God's, then in verse 36 says that if this is boasting he will boast. The argument is settled by relocating the subject.

chapter.title: He quotes Alma's conversion at people who were there
chapter.text: Darkest abyss and marvelous light are Alma's words about himself in Mosiah 27. Ammon applies them to a nation and says nothing about the borrowing.

chapter.title: Knowledge is tied to repentance
chapter.text: Verse 21 puts the mysteries out of reach of the natural man and inside the reach of the penitent, and verse 22 makes the qualification a set of practices instead of a status.

chapter.title: The mission almost ended before it began
chapter.text: Verse 27 has them depressed and turning back. Fourteen years of results rest on a moment that could have gone the other way, and Ammon reports it in the middle of the celebration.

chapter.title: The cost is listed beside the harvest
chapter.text: Stoning, spitting, cords, and prison sit in the same speech as the sheaves and the garners. The chapter refuses to give the joy without the ledger.

chapter.title: He ranks his own nation second
chapter.text: No love like this in the land, not even among the Nephites, because Nephites fight back. It is a hard thing for a Nephite prince to say to Nephites.

chapter.title: The last verse is about everyone else
chapter.text: After a chapter on one mission, Ammon ends with God mindful of every people in whatever land, numbering them, mercy over all the earth. The particular success opens onto a general claim.

applications.title: Answer the correction instead of dismissing it
applications.text: Aaron told Ammon he was boasting, and Ammon took the word seriously enough to work out what he actually meant by it. When someone names a fault in how you are speaking, engage the word they used.

applications.title: Count the sheaves out loud
applications.text: Ammon told his co-workers to look at the number. Where a long effort has produced something, say specifically what it produced to the people who helped, instead of leaving it to be assumed.

applications.title: Keep going when the promise comes with a condition
applications.text: The success was promised on the other side of patient affliction. When the encouragement you get is that it will be worth it and hard, treat that as an answer.

applications.title: Correct yourself in public
applications.text: Ammon said the mercies of the world and then fixed it mid-sentence. When you hear yourself say something slightly off, say the better version right there rather than letting it stand.

questions.text: What have I labored at long enough to be able to count the result?
When someone last told me my enthusiasm had gone somewhere wrong, what did I do with it?
What would it change if I said out loud that I am nothing and meant it as a fact rather than as self-criticism?
What do I feel about God that I cannot say the smallest part of?
Which of the four things in verse 22 am I currently not doing?
What am I on the edge of turning back from?
Whose love have I been slow to admit exceeds my own people's?

entries.head: Alma 17:11
entries.reason: the commission as it was first given, with the same condition

targets.quote: ye shall be patient in long-suffering and afflictions,
targets.verse_text: And the Lord said unto them also: Go forth among the Lamanites, thy brethren, and establish my word; yet ye shall be patient in long-suffering and afflictions, that ye may show forth good examples unto them in me, and I will make an instrument of thee in my hands unto the salvation of many souls.
targets.markdown: And the Lord said unto them also: Go forth among the Lamanites, thy brethren, and establish my word; yet **ye shall be patient in long-suffering and afflictions**, that ye may show forth good examples unto them in me, and I will make an instrument of thee in my hands unto the salvation of many souls.

entries.head: Alma 24:18

anchor.quote: they have buried their weapons of war deep in the earth

entries.reason: the covenant Ammon is pointing at as evidence of their love

targets.quote: they would give up their own lives;
targets.verse_text: And this they did, it being in their view a testimony to God, and also to men, that they never would use weapons again for the shedding of man's blood; and this they did, vouching and covenanting with God, that rather than shed the blood of their brethren they would give up their own lives; and rather than take away from a brother they would give unto him; and rather than spend their days in idleness they would labor abundantly with their hands.
targets.markdown: And this they did, it being in their view a testimony to God, and also to men, that they never would use weapons again for the shedding of man's blood; and this they did, vouching and covenanting with God, that rather than shed the blood of their brethren **they would give up their own lives**; and rather than take away from a brother they would give unto him; and rather than spend their days in idleness they would labor abundantly with their hands.

targets.verse_text: I know that which the Lord hath commanded me, and I glory in it. I do not glory of myself, but I glory in that which the Lord hath commanded me; yea, and this is my glory, that perhaps I may be an instrument in the hands of God to bring some soul to repentance; and this is my joy.

entries.head: Mosiah 27:29
entries.reason: Alma using both phrases of himself, with Ammon present
